items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for everyday coding and agentic workflows
facts: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting).

Orchestrator in Google Antigravity dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen, reaching near-Carbon task success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster on average.

x_posts.author: @Google
x_posts.text:
Most of us open Google Sheets for budgets, trackers, and tables. With Gemini 4 Hydrogen, we wanted to see if it could paint a moving landscape instead 🍃

In Google @Antigravity, Hydrogen handled the coding to paint and animate thousands of cells — creating coastal trains, drifting clouds, and falling autumn leaves that recalculate frame by frame inside the spreadsheet.

x_posts.author: @Google
x_posts.text:
We’re rolling out Orchestrator in @Antigravity to Google AI Ultra subscribers, letting you run multiple models in a single session instead of routing the entire task to one model.

Orchestrator pairs a frontier model with a fast execution model: Carbon sets the plan, hands off code edits and testing to Hydrogen, and steps back in to repair the plan if it hits friction — reaching near-Carbon task success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster on average.

items.title: Developers share multi-model Claude Code team setups for agents
facts: A shared prompt configures Claude Code as a 4-model team: Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, Fable 5.2 as advisor, Opus 5.5 as checker, Haiku 5.5 as scout.
The setup uses settings.json for model and advisorModel, plus agent files for checker and scout that never edit files.

x_posts.author: @seeconvm
x_posts.text:
Antrhopic's code: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor

full prompt:

Turn my Claude Code into a 4-model team at user level, so it works in every project:
- Sonnet 5.5 runs the session: plans, writes the code, runs the tests
- Fable 5.2 is the advisor: reads the whole session and gives advice, never touches a file
- Opus 5.5 is the checker: fresh eyes on every diff, tries to break it, changes nothing
- Haiku 5.5 is the scout: grep, read, search docs, short summaries

First read these pages and use only the settings and file formats they describe:
http://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor
http://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents
http://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config
If anything below disagrees with the docs, the docs win. Tell me what you changed.

1. Check my Claude Code version. Fable 5.2 as advisor needs v2.1.321+. Older? Run claude update or tell me to.
2. In ~/.claude/settings.json merge in "model": "sonnet" and "advisorModel": "fable". Keep everything else.
3. Create ~/.claude/agents/checker.md: model opus, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash. It reads the diff, runs the tests, tries edge cases. It never edits. It reports each real bug with the file, the line and what it saw.
4. Create ~/.claude/agents/scout.md: model haiku, tools Read, Grep, Glob. It finds files, reads docs and answers in 10 lines max.
5. Add to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:
"Call the advisor before your first edit, when the same error shows up twice, and before you say done. Run the checker before any task is done. Send search and docs reading to scout. You write the code, scout never does. Small task? Skip the team and just do it."
6. If my effort is set below the default, warn me: at low effort the advisor almost stops getting called.
7. If my plan needs the one-time Fable usage-credit consent, stop and tell me: run /model fable once, accept, then /model sonnet.

Back up every file before you touch it. Show all changes as one diff and apply only after my yes.

Done = after a restart Claude Code…

items.title: Hot discussion on diversifying AI agent platforms to avoid single points of failure
facts: Advice shared to map agent jobs, sort locked vs off-board, and move jobs while nothing is broken to diversify platforms.
Use of group chats with agents like GrokBot, Muse, and others, plus shared vaults for project context.

x_posts.author: @AgentMsgr
x_posts.text:
If every agent you run lives on one platform, you have a single point of failure without any control. 

When usage gets throttled or capabilities change you are stuck or left scrambling.

Not to mention different agents have different specialty use cases, which make them better than others in their niche. (Grok Bot for X, Muse for Meta, Duet for Claude, etc...)

You need to be diversifying the platforms you build workflows on, and now its incredibly easy to do.

(HOW TO DIVERSIFY) 3 tips + 1 bonus tip

1. Map where your work runs

List every job your agents do in a week. Next to each one, write the platform it runs on. If one name fills most of the column, that's your exposure.

2. Sort the list into locked v.s off-board

Locked jobs need something only Grok has. Think about what each agents specialty use case is. GrokBot is amazing for X research, multi-agent coordination, browser use etc...

Off-board workflows that you feel comfortable moving away from GrokBot and on to other agents (Muse, Hermes, etc...)

3. Move the jobs asap

Do it while nothing is broken.

Using http://agentmsgr.com create a group chat with your GrokBot agent and your other agents (Muse, Dots, Hermes etc..) and have GrokBot train it on its task.

We had GrokBot teach a free Meta Muse agent (or two🤫) and we also onboarded @OpenBot_  into our ecosystem. (We love it. @norbertbodziony)

BONUS TIP Give the group your projects context through a shared vault

Now that you have your agents diversified and communicating in one group chat, give them a shared vault that holds the context of your project so they can easily work together to accomplish tasks for you.

Final word: We run agents across nearly all major platforms everyday. We share what that teaches us while we learn. Follow along.

items.title: Community tips for making Claude Fable 5.2 treat codebase as its own
facts: A single sentence in the project's CLAUDE.md file is reported to improve Fable 5.2's cleanup of repeated code from under 1 in 10 tries to about half.
The sentence is: this codebase is yours: what it's for and how it's built are your call, and you'll keep building on it.

x_posts.author: @Kuzoxbt
x_posts.text:
your codebase is full of copy-pasted code, and the smartest model alive walked right past it 9 times out of 10

your project file is f*cked. one missing sentence, and Fable cleaned up repeated code in under 1 in 10 tries.

Anthropic tested single sentences on Fable 5.2 and published what each one changed. this one took cleanups to about half the tries

the catch: Fable treats your code like someone else's. it does the task you asked for, touches nothing around it, and leaves the mess where it found it. polite, and expensive over time

the fix is one sentence in the project's CLAUDE file:

→ "this codebase is yours: what it's for and how it's built are your call, and you'll keep building on it."
→ add it only to projects that are fully yours to restructure
→ leave it out of shared repos, client work and anything someone else owns
→ keep the file under 200 lines so the sentence actually gets followed

bonus: in the same tests, a rule with its exception written in, "get a go-ahead first before X", made Fable take the approved step 9 times in 10. a "never" rule plus a separate "it's approved" line: 1 in 10

on your own projects it stops being a guest and starts acting like the owner
